test_cases.title: Create user persists bcrypt hash, never plaintext
test_cases.given: a valid create-user payload including a plaintext password
test_cases.then: the persisted password_hash column value is a bcrypt hash (identifiable bcrypt prefix), distinct from the submitted plaintext, and is never equal to the plaintext value

test_cases.title: Hash is unique per call due to bcrypt salting
test_cases.given: the same plaintext password hashed twice via AuthService.hash_password
test_cases.when: the two resulting hash values are compared
test_cases.then: they are not equal, confirming per-call random salting

test_cases.title: Verify succeeds for correct password
test_cases.given: a user record created with a known password
test_cases.when: AuthService.verify_credentials is called with the correct email and plaintext password

test_cases.title: Verify fails for incorrect password without leaking distinction
test_cases.given: a user record created with a known password
test_cases.when: AuthService.verify_credentials is called with the correct email and an incorrect plaintext password
test_cases.then: it returns false and no exception, log line, or response body reveals the submitted plaintext or distinguishes the failure reason

test_cases.title: Hash/verify failures logged at WARN with user id only
test_cases.given: a bcrypt/passlib exception is raised during hash or verify (simulated via a forced library error)
test_cases.when: the service layer catches the exception
test_cases.then: a WARN-level log entry is emitted containing the user id only, no plaintext or hash material appears in the log, and the API layer receives a generic readable error rather than a raw stack trace

test_cases.title: GET /api/users list response omits password fields
test_cases.given: at least one user exists in the system
test_cases.then: the raw JSON response body contains no 'password' or 'password_hash' key for any returned user object

test_cases.title: GET /api/users/{id} response omits password fields
test_cases.then: the raw JSON response body contains no 'password' or 'password_hash' key

test_cases.title: POST and PUT /api/users responses omit password fields
test_cases.given: a valid create payload and a valid update payload for an existing user
test_cases.then: neither response body contains a 'password' or 'password_hash' key

test_cases.title: Create user without password is rejected, no default invented
test_cases.given: a create-user payload that omits the password field entirely
test_cases.then: the request is rejected with a 422 validation error and no user record is persisted with an invented default password

test_cases.title: Create user with empty-string password is rejected
test_cases.given: a create-user payload with password set to an empty string
test_cases.then: the request is rejected with a 422 validation error

test_cases.title: Bcrypt hashing latency stays within p95 budget
test_cases.given: 100 distinct plaintext passwords hashed sequentially with work factor 12 under single-request, non-concurrent load
test_cases.when: hash latency for each call is measured
test_cases.then: p95 latency is <= 300ms; if exceeded, work factor is reduced to 11 and re-benchmarked per the documented tuning procedure

test_cases.title: Placeholder-hashed rows fail verification after bcrypt cutover
test_cases.given: a user row persisted with AUTH-02's pbkdf2_hmac placeholder hash format
test_cases.when: AuthService.verify_credentials is called against that row with the correct original plaintext
test_cases.then: verification fails (returns false) without raising an unhandled exception, confirming the documented expected incompatibility
